knowledge:
- key_parameters: object=A phyloseq or TreeSummarizedExperiment object containing the microbiome count data ;; models=A character vector specifying which parametric distributions to fit (e.g., "NB", "ZINB", "DM", "ZIG", "HURDLE") ;; scale_HURDLE=Scaling method for the Hurdle model ("median" or "default") ;; nsamples=Number of samples in the dataset ;; N=Number of mock or split iterations to generate ;; method_list=A list of DA method instructions generated by set_* functions ;; normalization_list=A list of normalization instructions generated by setNormalizations() ;; weights=Observational weights (e.g., from weights_ZINB()) used in GLM frameworks ;; priorKnowledge=A data frame containing prior biological information for enrichment analysis ;; enrichmentCol=Column name in priorKnowledge indicating the category (e.g., "Type") ;; namesCol=Column name in priorKnowledge matching the feature names ;; slot=The slot of the DA output list to use (e.g., "pValMat" or "statInfo") ;; colName=The column name of the slot to use (e.g., "rawP", "adjP", "logFC") ;; direction=Vector of column names in statInfo representing the direction of DA for each method
- alternatives: The documentation mentions various DA methods native to different fields (RNA-Seq, scRNA-Seq, Microbiome) that can be benchmarked, including edgeR, DESeq2, limma, NOISeq, dearseq, metagenomeSeq, corncob, ALDEx2, ANCOMBC (ANCOMBC2), linda, Maaslin2, maaslin3, mixMC, ZicoSeq, Seurat, and MAST. Non-parametric methods like ANCOM cannot be evaluated using the GOF framework but can be evaluated using TIEC, Concordance, and Enrichment.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have a microbiome count dataset (16S or WMS absolute counts) and want to systematically evaluate and select the most appropriate differential abundance detection method based on statistical fit, false positive control, reproducibility, and biological validity.
- pitfalls: Data pre-processing (QC, filtering, normalization) is not directly handled by benchdamic but is critical; users must perform these steps beforehand. ;; fitHURDLE output should not be compared directly to observed log(counts+1) mean values; instead, use the logarithm of observed CPM or median-scaled counts via prepareObserved(..., scale = "median"). ;; ANCOM-based methods are only compatible with SerialParam() (single core) due to internal parallelization management; running them with MulticoreParam() can cause issues. ;; Low mock iterations (e.g., N=3) lead to imprecise FDR and FPR estimates; at least N=1000 is suggested for TIEC, and N=100 for Concordance. ;; Some methods (like NOISeq and mixMC) do not return raw p-values, so they cannot be included in TIEC or p-value-based concordance analyses.

workflows.name: goodness_of_fit_assessment
workflows.intent: Assess which parametric distributions best fit the count data and zero proportions of a microbiome dataset.
input: ps_stool_16S (phyloseq object containing raw microbiome counts)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit a single model (e.g., Hurdle) to estimate counts and zero probabilities ;; 2. Prepare observed counts with matching scaling ;; 3. Compute mean differences and zero probability differences ;; 4. Fit multiple parametric models simultaneously ;; 5. Extract and plot Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Differences (MD)
workflows.code:
example_HURDLE <- fitHURDLE(
    object = ps_stool_16S,
    scale = "median"
)
observed_hurdle <- prepareObserved(
    object = ps_stool_16S, 
    scale = "median")
meanDifferences(
    estimated = example_HURDLE,
    observed = observed_hurdle
)
GOF_stool_16S <- fitModels(
    object = ps_stool_16S,
    models = c("NB", "ZINB", "DM", "ZIG", "HURDLE"),
    scale_HURDLE = c("median", "default"),
    verbose = FALSE
)
plotRMSE(GOF_stool_16S, difference = "MD", plotIt = FALSE)
plotRMSE(GOF_stool_16S, difference = "ZPD", plotIt = FALSE)
plotMD(
    data = GOF_stool_16S,
    difference = "MD",
    split = TRUE
)

workflows.name: type_i_error_control
workflows.intent: Evaluate the ability of various DA methods to control false positives using mock comparisons.
input: ps_stool_16S (phyloseq object containing raw microbiome counts)
workflows.stages: 1. Create mock groups by randomly assigning homogeneous samples ;; 2. Set up and run normalizations ;; 3. Filter rare taxa ;; 4. Compute zero-inflated negative binomial weights ;; 5. Set up DA methods and run them on mock comparisons ;; 6. Summarize Type I Error Control (TIEC) metrics ;; 7. Plot False Positive Rate (FPR), False Discovery Rate (FDR), QQ-plots, Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics, and p-value log distributions
workflows.code:
set.seed(123)
my_mocks <- createMocks(
    nsamples = phyloseq::nsamples(ps_stool_16S),
    N = 3
)
my_normalizations <- setNormalizations(
    fun = c("norm_edgeR", "norm_DESeq2", "norm_CSS"), 
    method = c("TMM", "poscounts", "CSS"))
ps_stool_16S <- runNormalizations(normalization_list = my_normalizations, 
    object = ps_stool_16S, verbose = TRUE)
ps_stool_16S <- phyloseq::filter_taxa(
    physeq = ps_stool_16S, 
    flist = function(x) sum(x > 0) >= 3, prune = TRUE)
zinbweights <- weights_ZINB(
    object = ps_stool_16S,
    K = 0,
    design = "~ 1",
)
my_basic <- set_basic(pseudo_count = FALSE,
    contrast = c("group", "grp2", "grp1"), 
    test = c("t", "wilcox"), 
    paired = FALSE, 
    expand = TRUE)
my_edgeR <- set_edgeR(
    pseudo_count = FALSE,
    group_name = "group",
    design = ~ group,
    robust = FALSE,
    coef = 2,
    norm = "TMM",
    weights_logical = c(TRUE, FALSE),
    expand = TRUE)
my_methods <- c(my_basic, my_edgeR)
bpparam <- BiocParallel::SerialParam()
Stool_16S_mockDA <- runMocks(
    mocks = my_mocks, 
    method_list = my_methods, 
    object = ps_stool_16S, 
    weights = zinbweights, 
    verbose = FALSE, 
    BPPARAM = bpparam)
TIEC_summary <- createTIEC(Stool_16S_mockDA)
cols <- createColors(variable = levels(TIEC_summary$df_pval$Method))
plotFPR(df_FPR = TIEC_summary$df_FPR, cols = cols)
plotFDR(df_FDR = TIEC_summary$df_FDR, cols = cols)
plotQQ(df_QQ = TIEC_summary$df_QQ, zoom = c(0, 0.1), cols = cols)
plotKS(df_KS = TIEC_summary$df_KS, cols = cols)
plotLogP(df_pval = TIEC_summary$df_pval, cols = cols)

workflows.name: concordance_analysis
workflows.intent: Measure the agreement between different DA methods (BMC) and within a single method (WMC) across split datasets.
input: ps_plaque_16S (phyloseq object containing raw microbiome counts)
workflows.stages: 1. Split the dataset randomly into two balanced subsets ;; 2. Set up normalizations and DA methods ;; 3. Run DA methods on the split subsets ;; 4. Compute concordance at the top (CAT) metrics ;; 5. Plot concordance dendrogram and heatmap
workflows.code:
set.seed(123)
sample_data(ps_plaque_16S)$HMP_BODY_SUBSITE <- factor(sample_data(ps_plaque_16S)$HMP_BODY_SUBSITE)
sample_data(ps_plaque_16S)$RSID <- factor(sample_data(ps_plaque_16S)$RSID)
my_splits <- createSplits(
  object = ps_plaque_16S,
  varName = "HMP_BODY_SUBSITE",
  paired = "RSID",
  balanced = TRUE,
  N = 2
)
my_edgeR_noWeights <- set_edgeR(
    group_name = "HMP_BODY_SUBSITE", 
    design = ~ 1 + RSID + HMP_BODY_SUBSITE, 
    coef = "HMP_BODY_SUBSITESupragingival Plaque", 
    norm = "TMM")
my_methods_noWeights <- c(my_edgeR_noWeights)
bpparam <- BiocParallel::SerialParam()
Plaque_16S_splitsDA <- runSplits(
    split_list = my_splits, 
    method_list = my_methods_noWeights, 
    normalization_list = my_normalizations, 
    object = ps_plaque_16S, 
    min_counts = 0, min_samples = 2, 
    verbose = FALSE,
    BPPARAM = bpparam)
concordance <- createConcordance(
    object = Plaque_16S_splitsDA,
    slot = "pValMat",
    colName = "rawP",
    type = "pvalue"
)
pC <- plotConcordance(concordance = concordance, threshold = 30)

workflows.name: enrichment_analysis
workflows.intent: Validate DA methods by checking if their significant findings are enriched for taxa known a priori to be differentially abundant.
input: ps_plaque_16S (phyloseq object containing raw microbiome counts)
microbial_metabolism (data frame containing prior biological knowledge of genus-level metabolism)
workflows.stages: 1. Integrate prior knowledge with the dataset's taxonomy ;; 2. Run normalizations and filter rare taxa ;; 3. Compute zero-inflated negative binomial weights ;; 4. Set up and run DA methods on the full dataset ;; 5. Perform enrichment analysis using prior knowledge ;; 6. Plot contingency tables, enrichment barplots, mutual findings, and true/false positive differences
workflows.code:
data("microbial_metabolism")
genera <- tax_table(ps_plaque_16S)[, "GENUS"]
rownames(microbial_metabolism) <- microbial_metabolism$Genus
priorInfo <- data.frame(genera, "Type" =  microbial_metabolism[genera, "Type"])
unknown_metabolism <- is.na(priorInfo$Type)
priorInfo[unknown_metabolism, "Type"] <- "Unknown"
priorInfo$Type <- factor(priorInfo$Type, 
    levels = c("Aerobic","Anaerobic","F Anaerobic","Unknown"), 
    labels = c("Aerobic","Anaerobic","F_Anaerobic","Unknown"))
priorInfo[, "newNames"] <- paste0(rownames(priorInfo), "|", priorInfo[, "GENUS"])
ps_plaque_16S <- runNormalizations(my_normalizations, object = ps_plaque_16S)
ps_plaque_16S <- phyloseq::filter_taxa(physeq = ps_plaque_16S, 
    flist = function(x) sum(x > 0) >= 3, prune = TRUE)
plaque_weights <- weights_ZINB(object = ps_plaque_16S, design = ~ 1,
    zeroinflation = TRUE)
my_edgeR <- set_edgeR(
    group_name = "HMP_BODY_SUBSITE", 
    design = ~ 1 + RSID + HMP_BODY_SUBSITE, 
    coef = "HMP_BODY_SUBSITESupragingival Plaque", 
    norm = "TMM", 
    weights_logical = TRUE)
my_methods <- c(my_edgeR)
Plaque_16S_DA <- runDA(method_list = my_methods, 
    object = ps_plaque_16S, weights = plaque_weights, verbose = FALSE)
enrichment <- createEnrichment(
    object = Plaque_16S_DA, 
    priorKnowledge = priorInfo, 
    enrichmentCol = "Type",
    namesCol = "newNames", 
    slot = "pValMat", 
    colName = "adjP", 
    type = "pvalue",
    direction = c("logFC"),
    threshold_pvalue = c(0.1),
    threshold_logfc = 0,
    top = NULL,
    alternative = "greater",
    verbose = TRUE
)
plotContingency(enrichment = enrichment, 
    levels_to_plot = c("Aerobic", "Anaerobic"), 
    method = "edgeR.TMM")
plotEnrichment(enrichment = enrichment, enrichmentCol = "Type", 
    levels_to_plot = c("Aerobic", "Anaerobic"))
plotMutualFindings(enrichment, enrichmentCol = "Type", 
    levels_to_plot = c("Aerobic", "Anaerobic"), n_methods = 1)
positives <- createPositives(
    object = Plaque_16S_DA, 
    priorKnowledge = priorInfo, 
    enrichmentCol = "Type",
    namesCol = "newNames", 
    slot = "pValMat", 
    colName = "rawP", 
    type = "pvalue",
    direction = c("logFC"),
    threshold_pvalue = c(0.1), 
    threshold_logfc = 0,
    top = seq.int(from = 0, to = 30, by = 3),
    alternative = "greater",
    verbose = FALSE,
    TP = list(c("DOWN Abundant", "Anaerobic"), c("UP Abundant", "Aerobic")),
    FP = list(c("DOWN Abundant", "Aerobic"), c("UP Abundant", "Anaerobic"))
)
plotPositives(positives)
